skill.name: gemini
skill.description: Guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Gemini CLI workflows for code review, plan review, and large-context software analysis. It covers model selection, approval modes, command templates, timeout use, and follow-up handling.
skill.summary: Runs Gemini CLI workflows for code review, plan review, and large-context analysis.
skill.author: softaworks

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown backticks around flags, model names, and code-fence delimiters, and those were marked false positive where no executable behavior exists. Confirmed risks come from the skill's intended Gemini CLI execution, repeated automated approval mode guidance, broad context sharing with an external service, and forceful process termination commands.

remediation.issue: Automated yolo approval mode is recommended for background tasks.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user consent before using yolo, prefer sandboxed or narrower approval modes, and document the exact tool permissions granted.

remediation.issue: Gemini CLI may receive broad repository or multi-directory context.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before sending private code, exclude secrets and generated files, and scope include-directories to the smallest necessary paths.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting commands include forceful process termination.
remediation.suggestion: Replace broad pkill examples with PID-specific steps that display the target process and ask for confirmation before kill -9.

semantic_findings.title: Automated Approval Mode Encouraged
semantic_findings.description: The skill repeatedly recommends --approval-mode yolo for background tasks, which auto-approves all Gemini CLI tools. This can allow broad file or tool actions without per-action review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly says yolo is for fully automated execution and required for background tasks. This is clear intent-level approval bypass risk, not just a syntax pattern.

semantic_findings.title: External Service Receives Broad Project Context
semantic_findings.description: The skill is designed to send large codebase and multi-directory context to Gemini CLI. Users could expose private source code, secrets, or proprietary documents if scope is not limited.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly targets entire codebases and additional directories, then invokes Gemini CLI. That strongly supports a data-exposure risk when repositories contain sensitive material.

semantic_findings.title: Forceful Process Termination Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The troubleshooting guidance includes pkill -9 and kill -9 commands. These commands can terminate the wrong process or destroy in-progress work if used without careful PID verification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are directly present and use forceful termination. They serve troubleshooting, but still carry operational risk in automated agent workflows.

content.user_title: Run Gemini CLI for Large Code Reviews
content.value_statement: Large codebases can exceed the context limits of a primary assistant. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through Gemini CLI model choice, approval mode selection, and result handling.
actual_capabilities: Guides model selection across Gemini 3 and Gemini 2.5 options.
Provides command templates for code reviews, plan reviews, and codebase analysis.
Explains approval modes for interactive, auto-edit, and background execution.
Includes timeout guidance and process checks for hung Gemini CLI sessions.
Supports multi-directory context through include-directories guidance.
limitations: Requires Gemini CLI v0.16.0 or later and configured Google credentials.
May send prompts and selected project context to Gemini through the CLI.
Does not provide built-in session resume support.
Automated approval modes can allow broad tool actions and need explicit consent.

use_cases.title: Review a large pull request
use_cases.description: Run Gemini over many changed files to identify security, performance, and maintainability issues.

use_cases.title: Validate an architecture plan
use_cases.description: Ask Gemini to examine a technical plan for scalability gaps, missing components, and integration risks.

use_cases.title: Map a legacy codebase
use_cases.description: Use large-context analysis to summarize structure, patterns, dependencies, and refactoring opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Gemini review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a focused review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gemini to review this project area for security and maintainability issues. Ask me before using automated approval mode.

prompt_templates.title: Plan review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gemini to review this architecture plan. Focus on scalability, missing components, integration risks, and simpler alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Large codebase analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for broad repository understanding.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gemini with only the relevant directories to analyze the codebase structure, conventions, technical debt, and refactoring options.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-directory risk review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request involving multiple project areas.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gemini to compare the backend and frontend directories. Produce prioritized risks, evidence, and suggested next steps.

output_examples.input: Review the authentication flow with Gemini.
output: Gemini found two session-handling concerns and one password policy gap.
The highest priority issue is missing token rotation after privilege changes.
Recommended next step: inspect the session middleware before making changes.

output_examples.input: Ask Gemini to review this architecture plan.
output_examples.output: Gemini returned a plan review covering scalability limits, data ownership questions, and deployment risks. The result includes prioritized follow-up questions.

output_examples.input: Use Gemini for a large-context repository overview.
output: Gemini summarized the main services, shared modules, and dependency boundaries.
It identified three refactoring candidates and two areas that need local verification.
The review recommends narrowing follow-up analysis to the billing and auth paths.

best_practices: Confirm the model and any high-impact approval mode with the user before execution.
Limit included directories to the smallest useful project scope.
Use timeouts for background runs and verify Gemini findings locally.
anti_patterns: Running automated approval mode without explicit user consent.
Sending an entire repository when a focused directory is enough.
Applying Gemini recommendations without reviewing evidence and tests.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides an assistant through Gemini CLI use for code review, plan review, and large-context analysis.

faq.question: Does it require Gemini CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The local Gemini CLI must be installed and configured with valid Google credentials.

faq.question: Can it modify files?
faq.answer: It can recommend approval modes that allow edits. The user should approve high-impact modes first.

faq.question: Is it suitable for private repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Prompts and selected context may be processed by Gemini through the CLI.

faq.question: Why does it mention timeout commands?
faq.answer: Timeouts help avoid hung background sessions when a command waits for unavailable approval prompts.

faq.question: Does it resume Gemini sessions?
faq.answer: No. The guide says follow-up analysis usually starts in a new Gemini session.
